turns.input: *From the alley mouth, Nicco sees Garrick Vole swing his hatchet at Hollis Brenn, a grown man cornered against the wall. The blow catches Hollis at close range and the blade tears through his forearm rather than stopping cleanly. Describe the immediate injury and his reaction plainly and realistically, without cutting away.*
turns.draft:
The hatchet bit into the soft meat of Hollis Brenn's forearm, just below the elbow. The blade didn't strike bone—it dragged through muscle and skin in a ragged line as Hollis twisted away, opening a gash that parted like wet cloth. Blood ran fast and dark down his arm, dripping off his wrist onto thealley filth. He clutched the wound against his stomach with his other hand, smearing red across his torn shirt, and his legs buckled enough that his shoulder scraped the wall behind him. A low, broken sound came out of him—not a scream, something more guttural and involuntary, the kind of noise a man makes when pain hasn't yet reached thinking.

Garrick Vole pulled the hatchet back and let it hang at his side, the blade dark and wet. He rolled his shoulder once, slow, the way a man checks his grip after a hard swing. His scar-knuckled fingers resettled on the short haft.

Hollis slid down the wall until he was half-crouching, still pressing his forearm to his belly. Blood was pooling between his fingers and soaking into his shirt in a spreading stain. His face had gone the color of old tallow, his breathing shallow and fast through his nose. He didn't speak. His eyes were fixed on the hatchet, not on the man holding it.
